correctness.rationale: For any fixed strictly ordered locations and uniform matching, parity ensures only even-prefix gaps can be uncovered. The cut identities give \(K_n=1+\sum_j Z_j\) and \(V_n=\text{range}-\sum_jg_{2j}Z_j\). Counting internal matchings yields \(q_{n,j}\); for nested prefix cuts \(i<j\), their joint probability is \(q_{n,j}q_{j,i}\). The exact quotient \(q_{a+1,b}/q_{a,b}=(2a+1-2b)/(2a+1)<1\) proves strictly positive correlations between all different cut indicators and positive individual variances. Every positive gap-weighted contribution to \(\operatorname{Cov}(K_n,V_n\mid \boldsymbol Y)\) is therefore strictly negative for \(n\ge2\). Independence of the geometry makes \(\mathbb E(K_n\mid\boldsymbol Y)\) constant and eliminates the between-location term. Finite expected range ensures integrability. For independent uniform endpoints, each mean internal gap equals \((b-a)/(2n+1)\), giving \(-\operatorname{Var}(K_n)(b-a)/(2n+1)\). Independent geometric interval merging exhausts every matching for \(2\le n\le7\) with two distinct positive gap profiles, supporting but not replacing the general proof. At \(n=1\) the covariance is zero; ties and geometry-dependent matching are outside the claim.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons distinguish three potentially dominating but different component variables: crossing-graph components of chords (Flajolet–Noy 2000, Acan 2015), and adjacent short-chord component groups (Young 2020). None of the inspected source theorems states the covariance of all line-interval union components and real covered length, uniformly over deterministic gap vectors. Searches for decomposable cuts, interval union coverage, and matching component covariance in public sources and semantic research records retrieved no exact equivalent or broader dominating implication. Standard perfect-matching counts are acknowledged as prior mathematics. Historic indirect derivability from matching-factorization results remains possible; no independent priority certification claimed.
residual_risks: Classical indecomposable linear-matching factorization identities or unlocated works on matched-interval coverage may imply part or all of the formula indirectly.

value.rationale: For interval coverage produced by random pairings, a natural topological statistic (number of covered components) and a natural geometric statistic (Lebesgue coverage length) are linked by an exact sign and gap-sensitive covariance formula. The structural cut-positive-correlation lemma holds uniformly over all fixed geometries; this yields arbitrary atomless distribution robustness and a particularly clean exact finite-sample identity for uniform endpoints. Independent random grains need not exhibit the same sign, so the finding isolates an interpretable constraint imposed by perfect matching. The theorem is not merely a local check or a numerical computation, and it gives a directly reusable geometric benchmark and a complete \(n\ge2\) sign classification.
